Maria B.: Heads up — noticed a sharp latency tail in prod right after the kernel-selector tweak this morning. Happens during short-lived burst traffic (chatty small requests) and correlates with a spike in KV-cache miss/eviction events. P95 went from ~120ms to ~420ms on affected routes.
AJ: Ugh. Which kernel path is being chosen when the spike happens?
Maria B.: The selector is picking FlashAttention v3 by default for most requests. Profiling shows v3 is great for long sequences/bigger batches, but when we get lots of tiny requests and KV misses force re-allocs, v3 ends up slower for those micro-batches.
Kevin L.: That matches microbench results last week — v3 has higher per-launch overhead and is sensitive to batch size and KV hot-path contention. Did you capture a flame/trace?
Maria B.: Yep. Pasting a small excerpt from perf dump:
```
# perf summary
route: /chat/stream (burst window)
seq_len: 32-64
batch_size: 1-4
kv_miss_rate: 0.28
kernel: flash_attn_v3
avg_token_ms: 9.8 (v3) vs 3.1 (v2)
call_overhead_ms: 4.6
mem_copy_ms: 1.2
```
AJ: Oof. So under high KV miss rate and tiny batches v2 is actually ~3x faster. We should consider a runtime fallback rule.
Sophia R.: Proposal: add a quick selector override: if batch_size <= 4 AND kv_miss_rate > 0.15 AND seq_len <= 64 -> prefer flash_attn_v2. Feature-flag it so we can toggle without deploy.
Kevin L.: +1. Also recommend temporarily increasing the threshold that triggers batching/coalescing for those routes (aggressive batching) — might help but risks added latency for cold requests.
AJ: Can we implement a conservative fallback in the selector without touching the kernel binary? Just selector logic change behind flag? If yes, low-risk.
Maria B.: Selector change only. I can prepare a PR that adds the conditional heuristic and exposes the flag `runtime.attn.selector_v3_fallback_for_small_batches` in the control plane. infra-bot: can we push a feature-flag change quickly?
infra-bot: Flag created: runtime.attn.selector_v3_fallback_for_small_batches (default: off). Can toggle per-route. Deploy to control plane config within ~10m.
AJ: Canary plan suggestion: enable for 5% of sessions on the affected route first, monitor p50/p95 and KV miss rate. If stable -> 25% -> 100% over ~2 hours. Keep rollback script ready.
Sophia R.: Add metrics to the alerting rule: sudden jump in kv_miss_rate OR p95 > 200ms should trigger paging channel and auto-disable flag for that route.
Maria B.: I'll open the PR with unit tests and a small synthetic sim harness to validate selector behavior under different batch/kv scenarios. Action items:
  - Maria: PR + sim harness (ETA 2h)
  - AJ: Canary rollout + monitor dashboard (ETA 1h)
  - Kevin: Short-term suggestion doc on batching threshold tradeoffs (ETA EOD)
  - Sophia: Add alert rule and test it in staging (ETA 3h)
infra-bot: Noted. Scheduled control-plane toggle window starting in 15m.
Maria B.: Thanks all. If the canary looks good we'll keep the flag as a guarded permanent heuristic and follow up with longer-term work: kernel launch overhead optimizations in v3 and smarter KV prefetching. :pray:
